Subject: Regional processing paths and 3rd-party network map

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for taking time earlier in the week. As part of our security intake we need a clear picture of where request data is processed when we call Redwood's hosted API. Specifically:

- Which cloud regions may touch inference requests (compute, KV cache, logging)?
- Which subprocessors or partner networks might see any portion of a request or telemetry?
- If we pin to a region (US-East), what guarantees do you provide and what fallbacks exist if capacity is constrained?
- Do any cross-border transfers occur for parts of the request lifecycle (billing, analytics, model updates)?

A worksheet or inventory that maps each processing step to regions/subprocessors would be ideal. We also need a sense of retention for request logs and any cached state.

Can you send an initial response + any artifacts we can share internally (one-pager, inventory CSV)?

Appreciate it — we have a compliance review next Wednesday.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Li
Head of Security Engineering
Novum Health

Hi Alex —

Thanks for the clear ask. I attached a short regional summary (redwood-regions-summary.pdf) that sketches which regions and services are involved by default for hosted API requests.

High level answers up front:
- Compute: requests are routed to the regional cluster selected by your account (default: us-east-1). If you pin to a region we keep inference compute inside that region except for limited automated fallback events (see note below).
- KV cache & prefix caching: stored in-region where compute runs; cross-region cache reads only happen during failover or if you configure global cache mode (not enabled by default).
- Telemetry/logs: application-level telemetry (traces, error events) are sent to a telemetry ingestion tier that is regional but may fan out to a central analytics cluster for aggregated metrics and billing.
- Billing & billing analytics: processed in our central billing region (us-west-2) which is needed for accounting/split & marketplace integrations. Billing records do not include full request content.

I'm looping in Karthik (infra) for the subprocessor inventory and precise fallback behavior — he'll attach the CSV with the partner list and network hops.

If helpful, we can also produce a per-endpoint worksheet that maps each pipeline stage to services and retention windows.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alex Li <alex.li@novumhealth.com>, tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 30 Jul 2028 08:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Regional processing paths and 3rd-party network map

Alex —

Attaching the subprocessor inventory (subprocessor-inventory.csv). Notes and clarifications below (short, since the CSV has the mapping):

1) Primary processing path (normal operation, pinned region = us-east-1):
   - Inference compute: us-east-1 (Redwood-managed GPU fleet).
   - KV cache: us-east-1 (Redis-compatible, managed by Redwood).
   - Persistent logs (request metadata, traces): retained in us-east-1 for 30 days by default (configurable).

2) Telemetry aggregation & analytics:
   - Aggregated metrics are periodically replicated to our analytics cluster in us-west-2 for product telemetry and billing reconciliation. These are aggregated counters and do not include raw prompts.
   - Subprocessors involved: DataMetrics Inc. (aggregation pipeline), CloudStorageCo (longer-term storage for aggregated metrics).

3) Failover and cross-region behavior:
   - If us-east-1 experiences prolonged capacity shortage or an outage, our smart routing may route traffic to a compatible regional pool (commonly us-west-2 or eu-west-1) depending on policy and customer configuration.
   - For customers requiring strict residency we recommend Dedicated or Private deployments. Hosted accounts can opt into strict-region pinning with an SLA exception and automated capacity controls (we'll document options in the deal).

4) Model updates and model store: models are pulled from our model registry located in us-west-2; model artifacts can be replicated to region-local caches. Pulling artifact metadata (version, checksum) does not include request data.

5) Billing & legal requests: billing records are consolidated in us-west-2; legal/DMCA/subpoena processes are handled per our policy, cross-border disclosures follow our privacy and export-control processes (details in the SOC2 + legal pack).

6) Data deletion & retention: see Marissa's note (below) for timelines.

Quick answers to your bullets:
- Which regions may touch inference requests? Primarily the pinned region and (rarely) configured fallback regions; analytics/billing regions for aggregated metadata.
- Which subprocessors might see portions? See CSV; key third parties are monitoring/metrics providers and long-term aggregated storage partners.
- Cross-border transfers? Possible for aggregated telemetry and rare failover routing — not for raw prompt storage unless you opt into global features.

If you need a stricter commitment, we can scope Dedicated capacity for Novum or a Private deployment. Happy to run those options through SOW.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Regional processing paths and 3rd-party network map

Thanks Karthik — that helps. Couple of follow-ups:

- For the KV cache: is any cache snapshotting or persistence replicated outside the pinned region? We run PHI-sensitive workloads and need guarantees about cache persistence and backups.
- For aggregated telemetry: can you confirm examples of the CSV fields that are replicated (e.g., request_count, error_rate, per-model token counters) and confirm that replicated artifacts never contain prompt text or user identifiers?
- Retention: we will likely need a 90-day configurable retention window for request metadata and a 0-7 day window for any caching of prompt-derived tokens. Is that configurable?

Also, please attach any deletion playbook or runbook we can reference in our intake.

—Alex
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Li <alex.li@novumhealth.com>
Cc: tessa_morgan@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 31 Jul 2028 15:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Regional processing paths and 3rd-party network map

Hi Alex —

Quick answers and references:

- KV cache persistence: cache is in-region by default and snapshots/backups are disabled for hosted accounts running PHI unless explicitly enabled. We do not replicate cache snapshots cross-region unless you request cross-region backup for resilience. I have flagged the CSV to show which customers have cross-region backup enabled; for Novum we can keep backups off.

- Replicated telemetry fields: the analytics replication contains aggregated counters (request_count, model_id, token_counts_by_bucket, error_rate) and anonymized performance metrics. We never replicate raw prompt text or full user identifiers. The CSV we provided has a column showing data type exposure for each subprocessor.

- Retention configuration: yes — request metadata retention is configurable up to enterprise limits. Default hosted retention is 30 days, but we support 7/30/90/365 day tiers for metadata. Cache eviction windows are configurable down to minutes and up to 7 days; prompt-derived state persisted in caches is ephemeral and can be set to 0-7 days per your requirement.

- Deletion playbook: attached (deletion-playbook.docx). It includes our deletion request process, deletion timeline (30 days to purge from hot storage, 90 days to purge from backups unless expedited), and proof-of-erasure flow we can run for audit. For dedicated/private customers the timeline can be tightened in contract.

Next steps: If you want formal guarantees we can put region-pinning + retention tiers into the SOW and include a carve-out that prevents automated cross-region fallback except under emergency DR (with customer approval).

Happy to hop on a short call with your security team to walk through the CSV and deletion playbook — when are you available?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Principal Product Security
Redwood Inference
